system_description.narrative_title: Middle East conflict driving oil-market disruption
system_description.narrative_summary: Escalation between Iran-backed Houthi forces, Saudi-led responses, and broader Iran-related tensions is disrupting shipping through key chokepoints (Hormuz, Red Sea) and striking energy infrastructure, prompting military deployments and regional offensives. Those security shocks, together with OPEC+ output choices and reserve releases, are producing mixed signals for global oil supply and prices—exports and inventories sometimes recover while shipping and production risks persist. The interplay of military, political, logistical, and market responses creates reinforcing feedbacks that amplify volatility in energy markets and regional instability.
system_description.scope: Physical oil and gas supply chain (production, pipelines, tankers, chokepoints like the Strait of Hormuz and Red Sea), regional state and non-state military actions (Saudi coalition, Houthis, Iran proxies), market mechanisms (prices, inventories, OPEC+ quotas, strategic reserve releases), shipping/logistics and insurance, and external policy tools (sanctions, military deployments).
system_description.super_system: Global political-economy and energy-security complex (world energy markets embedded in geopolitical stability and international trade flows)
adjacent_subsystems: Global oil & financial markets (trading, futures, commodity risk)
Regional Middle East security and proxy conflict dynamics
Maritime shipping, logistics and insurance markets
National energy policy and strategic petroleum reserve management

variables.name: Chokepoint throughput
variables.description: Rate of oil and gas shipments transiting key maritime chokepoints per unit time.

variables.name: Tanker security risk
variables.description: Probability-weighted exposure of tankers to attacks, interdiction, or hostile incidents in transit corridors.

variables.name: Energy infrastructure damage rate
variables.description: Rate at which production, refining, or storage facilities sustain damage or outages due to hostile or accidental events.

variables.name: Production capacity utilization
variables.description: Fraction of installed upstream production capacity actively producing hydrocarbons at a given time.

variables.name: Spare production capacity
variables.description: Volume of producible hydrocarbon capacity that is currently idle and could be brought online within a short timeframe.

variables.name: Crude inventory levels
variables.description: Total onshore and floating stocks of crude oil held in commercial and strategic storages.

variables.name: Strategic reserve release rate
variables.description: Rate at which strategic petroleum reserves are being drawn down and released into the market.

variables.name: Producer output policy stance
variables.description: Degree of coordinated producer-side restraint or augmentation of crude output as a policy posture.

variables.name: Shipping insurance premium level
variables.description: Market cost level for insuring tanker voyages in exposed regions, expressed as a premium multiplier or rate.

variables.name: Shipping delay rate
variables.description: Average additional transit time or frequency of voyage delays experienced by tankers due to security or routing disruptions.

variables.name: Global oil price level
variables.description: Representative market price level for benchmark crude grades observed in global trade.

variables.name: Oil price volatility
variables.description: Magnitude of short-to-medium term fluctuations in oil prices measured by realized or expected variance.

variables.name: Market supply-risk perception
variables.description: Aggregated market and trader perception of current and near-term risk to physical oil supply reliability.

variables.name: Freight rate levels
variables.description: Average shipping freight rates for crude and petroleum product tankers on major routes.

variables.name: Sanctions enforcement intensity
variables.description: Degree and strictness of trade-restricting measures applied to actors and flows relevant to hydrocarbon trade.

variables.name: Military deployment intensity
variables.description: Scale and concentration of military forces and operations in and around energy transit corridors and producing regions.

catalysts.title: Planned Saudi assault on Houthis
catalysts.description: A reported Saudi plan to assault Houthi positions to break the Red Sea chokehold could trigger intensified strikes, naval operations and wider disruption to shipping.

catalysts.title: Mecca Pact committee meeting in Riyadh (Oct 5)
catalysts.description: Emergency Mecca Pact talks in Riyadh may coordinate regional responses to Houthi attacks and shipping security, influencing deployments and sanctions stances.
catalysts.rationale: [2026-10-02] Pakistan says Mecca pact members to hold emergency talks; [2026-10-04] Turkey says Mecca pact committee to meet Oct 5

catalysts.title: OPEC+ to keep November output steady

catalysts.title: US deploys additional carrier group and troops
catalysts.description: US dispatch of a third carrier group and thousands of troops to the region increases military presence and alters security dynamics around transit corridors.
catalysts.rationale: [2026-10-02] U.S. to send third carrier group; [2026-10-02] US deploys thousands of troops to Middle East

catalysts.title: Iran conditions keep Strait of Hormuz restricted
catalysts.description: Iran's statement that the Strait of Hormuz will not reopen until conditions are met implies prolonged restrictions or conditional access, sustaining transit risk.
catalysts.rationale: [2026-10-04] Iran says Strait of Hormuz will not reopen until conditions are met

catalysts.title: Resurgence of tanker attacks in transit corridors
catalysts.description: Recent projectile and strike incidents on tankers off Hormuz and Oman signal a renewed pattern of attacks, raising immediate shipping risk and insurance costs.
catalysts.rationale: [2026-10-02] Three oil tankers hit; [2026-10-03] Crude oil tanker struck off Oman; [2026-10-04] More tankers struck

catalysts.title: Strate gic reserve draws and announced releases
catalysts.description: IEA and national reserve release decisions and rising U.S. crude stocks indicate coordinated or market-driven inventory releases that can ease prices short-term.
catalysts.rationale: [2026-10-02] IEA's Birol says prices starting to fall after reserve release decision; [2026-10-02] U.S. Crude Oil Stockpiles Jump

catalysts.title: Yemeni government offensive vs Houthis
catalysts.description: An offensive to seize Houthi-held areas increases local combat, risks strikes on facilities and could expand maritime interdiction or retaliation.
catalysts.rationale: [2026-10-04] Yemeni government launches offensive to seize all areas from Iran-backed Houthis

catalysts.title: OPEC+ delays capacity review and expansion plans
catalysts.description: Reported postponement of OPEC+ capacity reviews and disrupted expansion plans slows growth in spare capacity, tightening medium-term market balance.
catalysts.rationale: [2026-10-02] EXCLUSIVE: OPEC+ delays oil capacity review after Iran war disrupts expansion plans
